Healing and Medical Care.text: Quirk healing is rare, hard to train and never free, so ordinary medicine does most of the work of keeping heroes alive. At U.A. Academy, Recovery Girl heals injuries with a kiss that speeds the patient's own healing; it draws on the patient's stamina, so a badly hurt student wakes exhausted, and she refuses to keep patching anyone who returns from the same recklessness, leaving them to mend the slow way. She cannot regrow what is lost or cure illness. Elsewhere ambulances, hospitals and doctors work as they do anywhere in Japan, with Quirk specialists at the big hospitals for injuries caused by Quirks and for patients whose bodies follow unusual rules. Recovery takes real time: a broken bone means weeks in a cast or splint, a concussion means rest and no training, burns need their dressings changed. Pros carry first aid kits, and larger agencies keep a doctor on call. Every Quirk injury treated at a hospital is reported to the police, so villains avoid hospitals and pay unlicensed doctors found through brokers. Hospitals post guards on patients under arrest, and a hero hurt in the line of duty gets a stream of visitors, flowers and cameras at the entrance.
